info.title: ulka-vms API
info.summary: Upload, encode, protect and play video from your own servers.
info.description:
Send an API key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Each key can use only the products it was given, at read or read-and-write; a key without the permission an operation names gets `insufficient_scope`.

Errors are JSON `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}`. Codes are stable: match on them, not on the HTTP status or the message. The message is plain words you can show your users as they are. Lists come as `{"data": [...]}`; the ones that grow long are paged newest first with `limit` and `cursor`, and return `next_cursor` and `total`.

tags.name: Videos
tags.description: Upload, import and manage videos, and follow them through processing.

tags.name: Playback
tags.description: Signing keys and signed addresses, and the player host's addresses: a video plays at `<player>/{library}/{video}`.

tags.name: Workspace
tags.description: Who is calling, usage, limits, notices and the API's own rules.

post.description: Reserves an upload. Send the file to `upload_url` with PUT (see the next operation), then create a video from it with POST /v1/assets (before or after the file arrives).

201.description: The upload is waiting for its file.

get.summary: See how much of a file arrived
get.description: How much of an upload's file has arrived, so a transfer that broke carries on from `received` instead of starting again. Like sending, it needs no API key: the upload's address is the permission.

put.description:
Sends the file for an upload from POST /v1/uploads. No API key is needed, so a browser can do it: the upload's address is the permission. It works until `expires_at` and until the file has arrived whole, and the file may be as large as `max_size`.

Send the whole file in one request (`curl -T video.mp4 <upload_url>`), or, for large files and shaky connections, in parts: each part is one PUT with `Content-Range: bytes START-END/TOTAL`, in order. A part starting at 0 starts the upload over; any other must start at `received`. If a part breaks, GET the same address to learn how much arrived and carry on from there. The part that completes the file starts the video's processing.

parameters.name: Content-Range
parameters.description: Only when sending in parts: which bytes this part is, and the whole file's size, as `bytes START-END/TOTAL` (END inclusive), e.g. `bytes 0-52428799/734003200`. Without it the body is the whole file.

200.description: The part arrived. `complete` says whether that was the whole file.

post.description: Creates a video from a direct upload (`upload_id`) or by importing a file from a public address (`input_url`); send exactly one. Processing starts once the file is in. Optionally sets who may watch (`playback_policy`); without it, the library's default.

get.description: Pages through the workspace's videos, newest first. `q` matches the title, reference (`passthrough`) or id; `status`, `library_id`, `folder_id`, `policy` and `trashed` filter.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only videos in this state (`waiting`, `processing`, `ready`, `complete` or `errored`), or in any of several, comma-separated.

parameters.name: folder_id
parameters.description: Only videos directly in this folder, or in a library's Home with `root`. Absent: the whole library, folders included.

parameters.name: policy
parameters.description: `public`: videos with a public link. `signed`: private videos, which have signed links and no public one.

parameters.name: trashed
parameters.description: `true` lists the trash instead of live videos.

parameters.name: metadata_key
parameters.description: Only videos with this metadata key, holding `metadata_value` (empty if not given).

200.description: One page of videos, newest first.

get.description: Returns a video's state, planned renditions, encoding progress, who may watch and its addresses.

delete.description: Deletes a video and all its stored files. Playback stops at once; files are removed in the background.

patch.summary: Rename, move or change who can watch a video
patch.description: Changes a video's title, who can watch it (`playback_policy`: every link it has changes policy and keeps its address, so embeds carry on; a video with no link gets one) and/or moves it to another folder or library. A move to another library with no `folder_id` lands in that library's Home.

folder_id.description: A folder id, or `root` for Home.

tags.description: Labels to find the video by (`GET /v1/assets?tag=`). Repeats, ignoring case, are dropped; no commas.

metadata.description: Your own key/value pairs, like your app's id for the video (`GET /v1/assets?metadata_key=&metadata_value=`). Keys are used once.

post.description: Starts processing again a video in status `errored` whose original file is still kept. Answers with the video, now `processing`. A video already processing answers as it is, so repeating the call is harmless. A video whose original is gone, or that didn't fail, is refused with `asset_not_retryable`; upload it again.

get.description: Returns the processing jobs for a video, newest first. Not paged.
Shows how the source file was read, the encoding plan, per-chunk progress, background tasks and stored bytes by folder. Meant for troubleshooting; the shape may grow.
Returns one processing job.

post.description: Creates a key for signing viewer tokens. The secret is shown only in this response.

201.description: The new key and its secret.

get.description: Pages the workspace's signing keys, newest first, without their secrets. `q` searches the key id.

delete.description: Deletes a signing key. Tokens signed with it stop working.

get.description: Shows where viewers download video segments from: this server, your own CDN, or a CDN the server runs.

put.summary: Choose where viewers fetch video from
put.description: This server, your own CDN in front of it, or a CDN the server runs where it offers one.

get.description: Counts the workspace's videos by state and totals playable minutes.

post.description: Adds an HTTPS address that receives every event in the workspace. The response holds the signing `secret`; it is shown only this once, so store it now.

201.description: The new endpoint, with its secret.

get.description: Pages the workspace's webhook endpoints, newest first, without secrets. `q` searches the address.

delete.description: Deletes the endpoint. Deliveries still waiting for it are dropped rather than sent.

get.description: One endpoint: its name, address, the events it receives and whether it is on.

patch.description: Renames it, moves it to another address, changes which events it receives, or switches it on or off. Its secret stays the same.

get.description: Pages what was sent to the endpoint, newest first, kept for 30 days. A failure is a plain sentence; the endpoint's own answer is never included.

200.description: One page of deliveries, newest first.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; empty on the last page.

total.description: How many rows match the filters, across all pages.

post.description: Puts a failed delivery back in the queue; it is tried again with the usual retries. A delivery already waiting answers the same way, so repeating the call is harmless.

get.description: The workspace, and what the caller may do in it. For an API key, `user` and `role` are absent and `permissions` come from the key's scopes; for a signed-in member they come from their role.

get.summary: The API's roles, products and limits
get.description: Roles and what each may do, the products API keys can be scoped to, and field length limits. Public and the same for everyone: nothing about any workspace.
What the workspace used in one calendar month (UTC): totals per meter, per day, and per region. Quantities only; no prices.

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: The month as `YYYY-MM`. Defaults to the current month (UTC).

get.description: The workspace's limits beside how much of each is used now.
Worked out from the workspace's current state on each request, so a notice disappears once its cause is fixed. Sorted danger, then warning, then info; within each, earliest `at` first. Not paged.

post.description: Asks for an MP4 copy of the video, made from its highest-quality rendition with sound, without encoding again. A finished video's is made now; one still processing gets it as soon as it finishes. Follow `download` on the video, or wait for `asset.download_ready`. Asking again while it's preparing or ready changes nothing.

202.description: The video, with `download` set to `preparing` (or already `ready`).

delete.description: Turns the download off and deletes its file. Playback is untouched.

post.description: Send the caption file itself as the body, WebVTT or SRT (SRT is converted), up to 1 MB. Players list it at once: every quality in the master playlist points at the new subtitles group. At most 20 tracks per video.

get.description: Oldest first.

delete.description: Players stop listing it on their next load of the master playlist.

get.description: Pages the workspace's libraries with their video counts and settings, newest first. `q` searches the name and description. A library groups videos and their folders.

200.description: One page of libraries, newest first.

post.description: A library groups videos and holds their settings. It starts with the workspace defaults.

get.description: Every folder of the library, flat; build the tree from `parent_id`.

post.description: In the library's Home, or inside `parent_id`.

get.description: One library with its video count and settings.

patch.description: Renames it, or changes its description, who can watch new videos, MP4 downloads or allowed distributions. A library following the workspace defaults stops following for what you change unless `inherit` says otherwise.

delete.description: Only an empty library that is not the default.

get.description: The ready-made presets, the library's own, and which one new videos use.

put.summary: Choose the preset for new videos
put.description: Videos already made keep how they were made.

post.description: A library's own preset: the sizes and how carefully they are made.

patch.description: Only the fields given change. Videos already made keep how they were made.

delete.description: Not while a library uses it.

patch.description: A folder can't move into itself or below itself.

delete.description: The folders below it go too, and their videos move to the trash.

post.description: They stop playing and leave lists; restore them, or they are deleted for good after 30 days.
Restore videos from the trash.
Only videos already in the trash.
To another library or folder, all or none.

get.description: What new libraries start with: player, preset, MP4 downloads, allowed websites and who can watch.

put.description: Libraries following the defaults change with them.

get.description: How the player looks and behaves for the library's videos.

put.description: Replaces them; a field left out goes back to its default.
Replaces the video's chapters as a whole (an empty list removes them). They are put in order by start; they can't overlap or run past the video's end. The player shows them on its timeline.

post.description: Signs a video's (or its whole library's) addresses with the workspace's newest signing key, exactly as your own server can: see the signature format under `GET /{library}/{video}/{file}`. Mint one per viewing and keep it short-lived.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: `playlist.m3u8`; a quality (`720p.m3u8`, `audio.m3u8`); `key`; `captions_<id>.m3u8` and `captions/<id>.vtt`; `poster.jpg`/`.webp` and `thumbnail.jpg`/`.webp` (`width`, and `time` for a thumbnail); `storyboard.vtt` and `storyboard.jpg`; `download.mp4`; `config.json` (the player's); `check.json` (what the viewer check needs: the server's time, the viewer's address and country, and whether this address would play, rule by rule; it answers even for an address that wouldn't play).

get.description:
Everything a video needs, on the player host, at `/{library}/{video}/…`; the watch page is `/{library}/{video}` itself. The address never changes, public or signed. Links inside playlists are relative, so a player follows them; a signed video's carry its token.

A **signed** video needs `?token=<signature>` on its address: `/{library}/{video}/playlist.m3u8?token=…`, or `/{library}/{video}?token=…` for the page. One signature covers every address its `acl` names: the playlists, key, captions, images and page. Make it on your server with a signing key from `POST /v1/signing-keys`:

1. `signed = "exp=" + <unix seconds> + "~acl=" + esc("/{library}/{video}/*") + "~kid=" + <key id>`, then optionally `"~ip=" + esc(<viewer address>)` and `"~wm=" + esc(<watermark>)`. `esc` is `encodeURIComponent`.
2. `signature = signed + "~hmac=" + hex(HMAC-SHA256(<key secret>, signed))`.

Put it in the address as it is, or URL-encoded once more (`URLSearchParams` does that); both work. `acl` is an exact path, or a prefix ending in `/*` (`/{library}/*` covers a whole library). `ip` limits it to one viewer address. `wm` is text Ulka's player shows over the video. Or let Ulka sign: `POST /v1/signed-urls`.

The watch page takes options after its address: `template` (see `GET /v1/player/templates`), then `autoplay`, `loop`, `muted`, `controls`, `preload` and `t`, each overriding what came before.

**Expiry:** starting playback (`playlist.m3u8`, `config.json`, `download.mp4`) needs a signature that hasn't expired. Everything a session fetches after that (qualities, the key, captions, pictures) still works for the video's length plus an hour past `exp`, so a viewer who started in time finishes the video. The signature itself (HMAC, `acl`, `ip`) is checked on every request.

200.description: The file: a playlist (`application/vnd.apple.mpegurl`), the 16-byte AES key (`application/octet-stream`, never cached), WebVTT, an image, or the player's config (`config.json`).

302.description: `download.mp4`: the file, with range requests for resuming.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The signature, for a signed video.

parameters.name: template
parameters.description: For `config.json` (the watch page passes it on): use this template's controls and start instead of the library's. See `GET /v1/player/templates`.

get.description: Ready-made controls and start behaviour for common uses: `standard` (every control), `minimal` (play, timeline, volume, full screen), `preview` (starts muted and repeats) and `background` (no controls, muted, repeats). Apply one by saving its `settings` into a library's player settings, or use it for one embed with `?template=` on the video's address. A template never changes the look (colour, theme, logo).

put.description: Makes the frame at `time` (seconds) the cover, `poster.jpg`/`poster.webp` on the player host and the player's picture before playing. `{"time": null}` goes back to the default frame, also after an uploaded picture. The cover is kept five minutes by browsers and CDNs.

time.description: Seconds from the start, within the length; null for the default frame.

200.description: The video, with its new cover.

put.description: The request body is the picture itself: JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF or HEIF/AVIF, up to 25 MB and 100 megapixels. It becomes the cover, kept as JPEG and WebP at most 1920 wide; `?width=` on `poster.*` resizes it. Choosing a frame again replaces it.

200.description: The video, with its new cover.

get.description: Plays the video over the network the way a player on another website does, from this server: the player's settings, the playlist, then for each quality its list, key, start and first piece (decrypted, so damaged files show), and each subtitle. Every answer must allow other websites (one `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`), or browsers refuse it. With `page`, the player's settings are asked as if embedded on that page, so the library's distribution lists apply. A private video is checked with a ten-minute signature from the newest signing key. Country rules are not checked: the requests come from Ulka's server.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The https address of a page the video is embedded on.

get.description: What viewers' own browsers found when they ran the check on the player host (`/{library}/{video}/check`), newest first, kept 30 days. A viewer who has trouble gives you the report's code. Each result is a step of the check: `id`, `state` (`ok`, `problem`, `note`, `skipped`), `ms` and `detail`.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The code a viewer gave you, like `UL-7K3M9Q` (any case).

get.description: Finds one of your workspace's viewer reports by its code, whichever video it is for. The same fields as a video's list (`GET /v1/assets/{id}/playback-reports`), plus `asset_id` and the video's `title`.

post.description: Explains whether the address a viewer used would play this video, and why not, the way playback decides: which video it names, its signature (format, signing key, match, what `acl` covers, expiry, a pinned `ip`), and the library's distribution and country rules for the page and viewer address given. Playback itself only answers `token_invalid`; this says which rule. Country rules need `ip` and the server's country database.

url.description: The watch page, playlist or file address the viewer used (with its `?token=`), or the bare signature.

page.description: The https address of the page it's embedded on.

country.description: The viewer's country (two letters), when `ip` was given and placed.

apiKey.description: An API key from the console's API keys page, or a signed-in session.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Where to continue: the `next_cursor` of the page before. Leave it out for the first page.

message.description: The code in plain words, fit to show a person. Wording may improve over time; match on `code`. Every code's words are in `messages` at GET /v1/meta.
message.example: That doesn't exist, or it was deleted.

expires_at.description: The file must be sent before this.

upload_url.description: Where to send the file, with PUT.

max_size.description: The largest file this workspace accepts, in bytes; a larger file is refused with upload_too_large.

upload_id.description: A direct upload's id. Send this or `input_url`.

input_url.description: Public http(s) address to import from, without a username or password. Send this or `upload_id`.

passthrough.description: Your own reference, returned as given and searchable.

playback_policy.description: Who may watch: `public`, or `signed` (needs a signed address). Without it, the library's default.

download.description: Also make an MP4 download once it's processed. Absent follows the library's setting.

library_id.description: Put the video in this library. Absent: the workspace's main library.

folder_id.description: A folder of that library, or `root` for its Home. Absent: Home.

status.description: `waiting` for the file, `processing`, `ready` (plays at lower qualities), `complete` (every quality), or `errored`.

input_url.description: Where it was imported from; null when uploaded.

renditions.description: Planned qualities; empty until the file has been read.

progress.description: Encoded chunks per lane: `fast` qualities play first, `full` finish the set.

playback_policy.description: `public` plays for anyone with the address; `signed` needs `?token=` with a signature (see `POST /v1/signed-urls`).

playback_url.description: The HLS playlist on the player host, `<player>/{library}/{video}/playlist.m3u8`. A signed video adds `?token=<signature>`.

embed_url.description: The watch page, for links and iframes. Player options go in the query: `autoplay`, `loop`, `muted`, `controls`, `preload`, `t`.

download.description: The MP4 download: null when off, `preparing`, `ready` (fetch it from `<player>/{library}/{video}/download.mp4`) or `failed`.

library_id.description: The library the video is in.

folder_id.description: The folder it is in; null when directly in the library's Home.

deleted_at.description: When it was moved to the trash; null while live. Trashed videos stop playing and are deleted for good after 30 days.

frame_rate.description: Frames per second, once the video has been read.

size_bytes.description: Size of the original file in bytes, once the video has been read.

timeline.description: The processing stages in order, with when each happened.

partial.description: How far the pieces being encoded now have got, in pieces (0.5 is half of one).

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; empty on the last page.

total.description: How many rows match the filters, across all pages.

problem.description: Why the last attempt to set the distribution up in this region didn't finish, in plain words, while it is still being tried or has failed. Absent otherwise.

source.description: The source file as read; null before it is read.

plan.description: How it is encoded; null before planning.

name.description: Top-level folder, or `playlists` for files beside them.

source_deleted_at.description: When the original file was deleted (after 30 days); renditions stay.

VideoStream.description: Fields that are empty or zero are left out.

secret.description: 32 random bytes, base64. Sign video addresses with the decoded bytes; the key id goes in `kid` (see the player host).

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; empty on the last page.

total.description: How many rows match the filters, across all pages.

mode.description: `origin` this server, `custom` your own CDN in front of it (`custom_url`), `ulka_cdn` a CDN the server runs itself, where it offers one.

custom_url.description: Your CDN's address when `mode` is `custom`; otherwise may be empty.

provider.description: For `custom`: which CDN it is, so the console can show its setup steps. `ulka` is Ulka CDN.

origin.description: Where your own CDN should pull from.

cdn_distribution.description: The distribution made for video on the CDN the server runs, once one exists.

serving.description: The segment address viewers get right now.

url.description: Must be https, with a host and no credentials. It must reach a public address; that is checked when delivering, not now.

events.description: The events sent here, from `webhook_events` in `GET /v1/meta`; empty for every event (the default), including ones added later.

WebhookDelivery.description: One event sent to one endpoint.

status.description: `pending` not tried yet, `retrying` tried and waiting for the next try, `done` answered with 2xx, `failed` stopped trying.

status_code.description: What the endpoint answered on the last try; null when it didn't answer.

failure.description: A plain sentence about the last failure; empty when none.

attempted_at.description: The last try; null before the first.

next_attempt_at.description: When the next try is due; set only while `retrying`.

events.description: The events sent here, from `webhook_events` in `GET /v1/meta`; empty for every event (the default), including ones added later.

secret.description: Signs deliveries. Shown only in this response.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; empty on the last page.

total.description: How many rows match the filters, across all pages.

id.description: Unique per event, and the same on every retry and for every endpoint; use it to ignore repeats.

WebhookAsset.description: A video as the API shows it.

error_code.description: Why it failed; null unless errored.

passthrough.description: Your own reference, as sent when the video was created.

input_url.description: Where it was imported from; null when uploaded.

playback_policy.description: `public` plays for anyone with the address; `signed` needs `?token=` with a signature (see `POST /v1/signed-urls`).

playback_url.description: The HLS playlist on the player host, `<player>/{library}/{video}/playlist.m3u8`. A signed video adds `?token=<signature>`.

timeline.description: The processing stages in order, with when each happened.

partial.description: How far the pieces being encoded now have got, in pieces (0.5 is half of one).

error_code.description: Why it failed; null unless failed.

user.description: Absent when calling with an API key.

last_login_at.description: When this person last signed in.

role.description: Absent when calling with an API key.

permissions.description: Each area the caller can use, at its highest level. Areas: video, cdn, images, webhooks, members, keys, workspace, owners. An API key only ever has the four products.

grantable_roles.description: Roles the caller may give others: none without members:write, otherwise every role up to their own. Always empty for an API key.

max_upload_bytes.description: The largest file this workspace may upload, in bytes (`upload_too_large` above it).

products.description: What API key scopes can grant.

key_ips.description: Most addresses on one API key.

ip_list.description: Most entries in a CDN distribution's allow or block list.

countries.description: Most countries in a CDN distribution's list.

referers.description: Most allowed referring websites on a CDN distribution.

headers.description: Most added or removed headers on a CDN distribution.

cache_path.description: Longest CDN cache rule path prefix, in bytes.

messages.description: Every code the API can report (errors, and why a video failed) in plain words, by code.

example.not_found: That doesn't exist, or it was deleted.

webhook_events.description: Every event a webhook endpoint can receive or choose, with its words.

player_url.description: The player host: videos are watched and streamed at `{player_url}/{library}/{video}` (`?token=` when signed).

console_url.description: Where the console is, so a page on the player host can tell the two apart.

player_demo.description: The video the player host's home shows, as `{library}/{video}`; empty when there is none.

period.description: The month: start included, end excluded.

totals.description: One row per meter with any use.

by_region.description: Only use recorded with a region.

max_upload_bytes.description: Largest single video upload or import.

encode_minutes.description: This month (UTC), including videos still encoding.

id.description: Stable across requests: the kind plus what it is about.

kind.description:
- `certificate_expiring`: a CDN distribution's certificate expires within 30 days. `warning`, or `danger` with 7 days or less left. Needs cdn:read.
- `certificate_expired`: it has expired. `danger`. Needs cdn:read.
- `deployment_failed`: a CDN distribution failed to deploy in a region (`data.region`). `danger`. Needs cdn:read.
- `domain_unverified`: checking a CDN domain's DNS record gave up without finding it; `name` is the hostname. `warning`. Needs cdn:read.
- `images_fallback`: over 5% (and at least 20) of a CDN distribution's image requests in the last hour were served unoptimized from its origin (`data.fallbacks`, `data.requests`, `data.reason`). `warning`. Needs cdn:read.
- `videos_failed`: videos errored in the last 7 days (`data.count`; `at` is the latest). `warning`. Needs video:read.
- `key_expiring`: an API key expires within 7 days. `warning`. Needs keys:write.
- `key_expired`: an API key has expired and can be revoked. `info`. Needs keys:write.
- `limit_encode_minutes`: 80% of the month's encoding minutes used (`data.used`, `data.limit`). `warning`, or `danger` at 100%. Needs video:read.
- `limit_cdn_distributions`: the CDN distribution limit is reached (`data.limit`). `info`. Needs cdn:read.
- `limit_image_sources`: the image source limit is reached (`data.limit`). `info`. Needs images:read.

subject.description: Id of what it is about: the CDN distribution for certificate, deployment and domain notices, the API key for key notices. Absent otherwise.

name.description: Readable name of the subject: distribution name, hostname or key name. Absent otherwise.

at.description: When it happened or will happen: expiry time, failure time, end of verification, or now for limit notices.

data.description: Extra numbers for some kinds; see `kind`.

VideoCaption.description: A caption track on a video, served as WebVTT and listed in its master playlist.

is_default.description: The workspace's main library; it can't be deleted.

mp4_downloads.description: Make an MP4 download for every new video.

allowed_domains.description: Websites allowed to embed the player; empty means any.

storage_bytes.description: Size of the originals of the live videos whose original file still exists.

by_status.description: Live videos by state: `ready` is `complete`; `processing` is `waiting`, `processing` and `ready`.

preset_template.description: The built-in transcoding preset new videos use, unless `preset_id` is set.

preset_id.description: The workspace's own transcoding preset new videos use; null when a built-in one is in use.

blocked_domains.description: Every website but these may show the player (an entry like *.example.com covers its subdomains). A library uses this or allowed_domains, not both: setting one non-empty empties the other.

country_mode.description: allow: viewers everywhere but `countries`; deny: only viewers in `countries`. Checked on the player and on every playlist and key, by the viewer's address.

countries.description: Two-letter country codes, like BD or US.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; empty on the last page.

total.description: How many rows match the filters, across all pages.

parent_id.description: The folder it is inside; null when directly in Home.

videos.description: Videos directly in it, not in folders below.

stream.description: The HLS playlist, relative to the video's address: `playlist.m3u8`.

storyboard.description: The scrubbing preview's index, relative to the video's address.

watermark.description: The signature's `wm`, verified: text to show over the video. Empty without one.

default_playback_policy.description: Who can watch new videos in this library: `public` anyone with the link, `signed` only with a signed address.

mp4_downloads.description: Make an MP4 download for every new video.

inherit.description: Per setting group, `true` follows the workspace defaults again (copying them in), `false` stops following.

mode.description: Where viewers fetch video from: `origin` this server, `custom` your own https address in front of it (`custom_url`), or `ulka_cdn` where the server offers one (see `modes`).

custom_url.description: For `custom`: your own https address in front of this server.

provider.description: For `custom`: which CDN it is, so the console can show its setup steps. `ulka` is Ulka CDN.

url.description: Must be https, with a host and no credentials. It must reach a public address; that is checked when delivering, not now.

events.description: The events sent here, from `webhook_events` in `GET /v1/meta`; empty for every event (the default), including ones added later.

end_time.description: Seconds; after start_time and within the video.

scope.description: `video` covers this video's addresses (`acl=/{library}/{video}/*`); `library` every video in its library (`acl=/{library}/*`).

ip.description: Only a viewer from this address may use it (`ip=`). Leave it out when viewers' addresses can change mid-watch (mobile networks).

watermark.description: Text Ulka's player shows over the video, like the viewer's email, so a screen recording shows who it was made for. Signed in as `wm`, so viewers can't change it. It deters leaks; it doesn't stop someone fetching the stream outside the player.

signature.description: `exp=<unix>~acl=<path>~kid=<signing key>[~ip=…][~wm=…]~hmac=<hex>`: goes in `?token=` on the video's addresses.

embed_url.description: The watch page, with `?token=`; add player options after it (`&autoplay=true`).

settings.description: Which controls show and how playback starts.

controls.description: Show the controls. Off: none at all, for a moving background or a page that drives the player itself.

autoplay.description: Browsers only allow it with the sound off.

skip.description: Seconds the back and forward buttons move; 0 hides them.

source.description: `default`: the frame at a tenth of the length; `frame`: one chosen with `PUT /v1/assets/{id}/poster`; `upload`: a picture sent to `PUT /v1/assets/{id}/poster/image`.

time.description: The cover frame's time in seconds; null for an uploaded picture, or before the length is known.

suggestions.description: Frames offered as covers (seconds), the default first; empty until the length is known. Each is `<player>/{library}/{video}/thumbnail.jpg?time=…`.

stage.description: `received`: processing began; `checked`: the file was read and planned; `playable`: the first qualities play; `complete`: every quality is ready.

at.description: When it was done (or failed); null while not done, or for videos processed before times were kept.

WebhookLive.description: The server or stream an event is about.

detail.description: The server's own description of what happened, when it gives one.

received.description: How many bytes have arrived, from the start of the file. Send the next part from here.

size.description: The whole file's size, as the first part declared it; null before any part arrived.

complete.description: The whole file arrived; the video starts processing as soon as it exists.

Error.description: The request was refused; `error.code` says why.

post.description:
A video was created from an upload or a URL import. `data` is the video.

Ulka POSTs each event to every webhook endpoint in the workspace; endpoints cannot choose events. An event is recorded in the same database transaction as the change it describes, so it is sent exactly when that change is saved, and only to endpoints that existed then.

**Request.** `Content-Type: application/json`, `User-Agent: ulka-webhooks`, and a `Ulka-Signature` header. The body is a `WebhookEvent`: `id`, `type`, `created_at` and `data`.

**Verifying.** `Ulka-Signature` is `t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>`, where `<hex>` is the HMAC-SHA256 of `<t>.<raw body>` keyed with the endpoint's whole secret, `whsec_` prefix included. Recompute it over the raw bytes you received, compare in constant time, and reject a `t` too far from your clock (for example over 5 minutes) to stop replays. `t` is fresh on each attempt; the body is not.

**Retries.** Any 2xx answer is success; the response body is ignored. Anything else, a connection failure, a redirect (they aren't followed) or no answer within 15 seconds is retried after 10 s, doubling each time up to once an hour, until 24 hours after the event, then dropped. So delivery is at least once and in no guaranteed order: use `id` to skip repeats. Deliveries go only to public addresses; a URL resolving to a private one always fails. Deleting an endpoint drops its pending deliveries.
The first renditions are published and the video can be played. Also sent just before `asset.complete` if it went straight there.
Every planned rendition is published. Its encoded minutes are counted in usage now.
Processing gave up before anything was playable; `data.error_code` says why. A video that was already playable stays so and gets only `job.failed`.
Sent as the video is deleted; `data` is the video as it was.
All the bytes of a direct upload arrived; processing starts next.
A direct upload wasn't finished in time and was discarded. The video's job then fails with `upload_expired`.
Ulka started working on a video's job (reading the upload, or fetching an import).
A video's job finished successfully.
A video's job gave up; `data.error_code` says why.

post.description: Its MP4 download can be fetched from `<player>/{library}/{video}/download.mp4` (with a signature for a signed video).

post.summary: A video's MP4 download couldn't be made
post.description: Making the MP4 download failed after retries; ask for it again with `POST /v1/assets/{id}/download`.
